sections.heading: C — Rules of the Road
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the Road

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A48
Use right-of-way sensibly rather than insisting on it; remain alert even when priority is yours. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A48
At a 4-way stop, every vehicle stops and the first arrival proceeds first. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A48
If adjacent drivers reach a 4-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on the right. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A49
Entering a public road from a private drive or road requires yielding to its vehicles and pedestrians without interfering with traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A49
A driver on an interstate entrance ramp yields to traffic already on the highway. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A49
When leaving a parked position, wait for moving traffic to pass. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A49
Never pass a vehicle stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A49
When vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, yield to the one on the right. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A49
Yield to vehicles that have already entered an intersection. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A49
A vehicle entering a traffic circle yields to vehicles already circulating. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A49
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren and flashing light, move immediately to the road’s right side, clear of intersections, and stop until it passes. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A49
Failing to yield as required to the described siren-and-flashing-light emergency vehicle is a Class E crime. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A49
A left-turning motorist yields to an oncoming cyclist or roller skier and turns only when safe without interfering with them. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A49
Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk when no traffic signal or police officer controls the intersection. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A49
While turning, yield to pedestrians crossing with the signal. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A49
Before crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway, stop and wait for pedestrians and traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A49
Always yield to schoolchildren who are crossing the street. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A50
Traffic controls include signals, signs, markings and directions from police, highway workers or school crossing guards. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A50
Do not drive through a parking area to evade a traffic-control requirement. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A50
A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow above green; a horizontal signal places red left, yellow middle and green right. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A50
A green light permits proceeding cautiously only when the route is clear of vehicles and pedestrians. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A50
A yellow signal warns of an approaching red phase and calls for slowing as the intersection clears. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A50
At red, stop before entering the intersection and remain behind the stop line or crosswalk until permitted to proceed. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A50
A right turn on red is allowed after a stop unless signs prohibit it, and the turning driver must yield to pedestrians and all vehicle traffic. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A50
At a flashing yellow light, slow down, proceed cautiously and be ready to stop for traffic. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A50
A flashing red traffic light requires stopping and checking both directions before entering. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A50
At a railway crossing with flashing red lights and barriers, wait until the flashing stops and the barriers rise before proceeding. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A50
With a red light and a green arrow, move cautiously only in the arrow’s direction while yielding to other vehicles and pedestrians. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A50
A steady yellow arrow clears turning traffic before red. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A50
A steady upward green arrow permits straight-ahead movement. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A50
A steady red turn arrow requires the indicated turning traffic to wait until the arrow becomes green. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A50
Where multiple traffic lights are present, follow the light directly above your lane. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A51
A steady red overhead X closes that lane to driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A51
A steady yellow overhead X means leave the lane because its signal is about to become red. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A51
A flashing yellow overhead X permits that lane only for a left turn. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A51
A green overhead arrow identifies a lane available for use. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A51
Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with black text or symbols that warn of hazards ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A51
A black cross on a yellow diamond warns of an intersection ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A51
A main vertical stroke with a side branch on a yellow diamond warns of a side road. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A51
A black T on a yellow diamond warns of a T-intersection. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A51
The yellow No Passing Zone pennant identifies a no-passing area. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A51
A winding black arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a curving road ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A51
A black right-curving arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a right curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A51
The divided-highway-begins warning shows opposing arrows separating around a divider. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A51
The divided-highway-ends warning shows opposing traffic beside a divider ending ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F46 | anchor: A51
The lane-ends warning depicts one lane boundary tapering toward the other. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F47 | anchor: A51
A diagonal branch joining an upward arrow warns of merging traffic. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F48 | anchor: A51
Two upward arrows separated by a dashed divider identify the illustrated added-lane warning. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F49 | anchor: A51
A traffic-signal picture on a yellow diamond warns that a traffic light is ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F50 | anchor: A51
A stop-sign symbol beneath an upward arrow warns that a stop sign is ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F51 | anchor: A51
The illustrated black chevron on yellow warns of a sharp curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F52 | anchor: A51
A curve warning paired with an advisory-speed plaque gives a suggested speed around that curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F53 | anchor: A51
The illustrated yellow school-zone pentagon contains two walking figures. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F54 | anchor: A51
The pedestrian-crossing warning shows a walking person on a yellow diamond. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F55 | anchor: A51
The Share the Road warning combines a bicycle, car and wording about sharing with bicycles. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F56 | anchor: A51
A bicycle pictured alone on a yellow diamond warns of a bicycle crossing. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F57 | anchor: A51
A car above wavy skid marks warns of a road that is slippery when wet. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F58 | anchor: A52
A round yellow railroad warning with a black X and RR calls for slowing, looking, listening and readiness to stop. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F59 | anchor: A52
A white railroad crossbuck marks a crossing where an approaching train requires stopping behind the line or before the tracks. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F60 | anchor: A52
Look for additional tracks and trains even when no track-count sign is posted. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F61 | anchor: A52
Look both ways and cross railroad tracks promptly without stopping on them. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F62 | anchor: A52
After a train crosses, wait until it is well down the track and any gates or lights indicate it is safe. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F63 | anchor: A52
When traffic or a signal requires a stop near tracks, wait at the stop line before the tracks. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F64 | anchor: A52
Work-zone warnings are orange diamonds or rectangles with black words or symbols. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F65 | anchor: A52
The illustrated work-zone warnings identify flaggers, workers, construction, a one-lane road and a detour. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F66 | anchor: A52
Follow a work-zone flagger’s directions. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F67 | anchor: A52
At a temporary traffic signal, stop at its white line if one is present. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F68 | anchor: A52
Barrels, cones, tubes and barriers identify restricted work areas, and a Road Closed barrier prevents entry. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F69 | anchor: A53
Slow down in work zones, avoid tailgating and be ready to stop promptly. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-F70 | anchor: A53
A speeding fine in a work zone is doubled. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

Misconceptions: a green light permits movement only when the route is clear. [A50]
Mnemonic: observe, yield, follow the assigned lane.
Glossary: regulatory signs direct matters such as turns, lanes and parking. [A53]
Dynamic facts: penalties and unusual lane controls retain their exact source scope.

items.why: Priority depends on arrival, road entry, pedestrians and emergency warnings.
Visual forms and signal states need a dedicated recognition surface.
Temporary controls and track-clearance decisions require distinct practice.
Color, broken/solid borders and lane assignment govern different movements.

corpus_stability.reason: Working assessment for the pinned Rev 4/24 snapshot: the frontmatter supplies one revision marker and this intake provides no evidence of more than annual revision. This is an inference for the fixed corpus, not a measured publication cadence; legal and administrative changes still require monitoring.
